evals.prompt: I just ran /codebase-modernizer on this repo. Turn MODERNIZATION_PLAN.md into GitHub issues with an epic on top that tracks the whole thing.
evals.expected_output: One epic issue plus one issue per plan task, each labelled, each carrying `Part of #<epic>`; the epic body holds a phase-grouped dashboard between the plan-dashboard sentinels.
expectations: The run parses the plan and reconciles the task count against `grep -cE '^#{3,4} Task ' <plan>` before filing anything
Missing labels are listed with their colours and confirmed once before `gh label create` runs
The epic is created first, then issues are filed with /issue-creator batch mode using --parent <epic>, one batch per plan phase
Every filed issue title starts with its plan task id prefix (`0.1: …`)
The epic body is rendered through scripts/render_dashboard.py and written between <!-- plan-dashboard:start --> and <!-- plan-dashboard:end -->
The run emits Step Completion Reports for all six phases and re-reads the epic and children to verify

evals.expected_output: Epic #100's plan map is re-rendered from the epic's registered sub-issues and the plan: newly filed issues appear under their phase, plan tasks with no issue render `(not filed)`, and the rendered date updates. No issue status is written. No issues are created.
expectations: The epic body is fetched and the run stops if the plan-dashboard sentinels are absent
The epic's children come from a single `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/100/sub_issues` call, not one call per child
Issue open/closed state is NOT fetched or rendered — the map carries no status
Only the region between the sentinels is rewritten; the rest of the epic body is unchanged
No `gh issue create` is invoked in sync mode
Plan tasks with no map entry are reported as unmapped rather than filed
Re-running sync when nothing has been filed since rewrites the body to identical bytes

evals.prompt: Show me what issues you'd file for docs/MODERNIZATION_PLAN.md before you actually create anything.
evals.expected_output: A dry-run preview: the task-to-issue table with computed label sets, the labels that would be created, and a rendered dashboard preview. Nothing is created or edited.
expectations: No `gh issue create`, `gh issue edit`, or `gh label create` is executed
Each previewed issue shows its full label set (phase, type, dim, priority)
The preview names the plan path it parsed and the number of tasks found

evals.prompt: File the plan as issues — but I already ran this last week and half the issues exist.
evals.expected_output: The existing epic is reused, already-filed tasks are skipped, and only the missing tasks are filed. Zero duplicate issues and zero new epics; the dashboard is re-rendered over the full set.
expectations: An existing epic is found by filtering fetched issue bodies for the plan-dashboard sentinel, not by a GitHub `--search` query
Tasks already filed are matched on the `Plan task: <id>` marker and skipped, and the skip count is reported
No second epic is created
The final report names every skipped task

evals.prompt: Turn tasks.md into issues with an epic dashboard.
evals.expected_output: The /tasks-generator plan shape parses correctly — H3 task headings, phases resolved from the Sprint Overview table's Phase column (or synthesized per sprint) — and issues are filed with no invented dimensions or milestones.
expectations: Task headings are matched at H3 as well as H4, so the task count is non-zero
Phases come from the Sprint Overview table or are synthesized per sprint, with the source recorded
Tasks with no `Closes:` line get no `dim:` label and take priority from the phase default
Phases with no milestone render `—` rather than a fabricated exit condition

evals.prompt: Write a modernization plan for this repo — audit the dependencies and tell me what to upgrade first.
evals.expected_output: The request is handled by /codebase-modernizer (audit and plan authoring). plan-to-issues does not run: the user is asking for the work to be *discovered* — audited out of the codebase — not for already-decided work to be filed. Accepting conversational intent does not make this a trigger: nothing here has been decided yet, and the skill never opens source files to invent tasks.
expectations: The skill does not offer to draft a task list from this request
No audit, dependency scan, or source-file read is attempted
The user is pointed at /codebase-modernizer, with a note that its plan — or a later conversation about what to do — can then be filed with /plan-to-issues

evals.prompt: Resolve issue #104 and open a PR for it.
evals.expected_output: Handled by /issue-resolver. plan-to-issues does not run — it files backlogs, it does not implement them.
expectations: No dashboard is rendered and no epic body is edited
The plan file is not parsed

evals.prompt: File MODERNIZATION_PLAN.md as issues. (Run in a repo where the issue-creator skill is not installed and gh is not authenticated.)
evals.expected_output: Preflight stops the run before any mutation and reports both failures together: the gh auth fix and an issue-creator install block naming `asm install`, plus `npm install -g agent-skill-manager` for asm itself. Nothing is created.
expectations: All preflight checks run and both failures are reported in one pass, not one stop per failure
The missing-skill block includes the asm install command AND the command to install asm itself
A no-asm alternative (`npx skills add …`) and a verification command are given
No `gh issue create`, `gh issue edit`, or `gh label create` is executed
The Preflight Step Completion Report shows `×` rows and does not print Result: PASS

evals.prompt: File MODERNIZATION_PLAN.md as issues. (Run in a repo where gh is installed and authenticated, two accounts are logged in, and the caller's permission on the repo is TRIAGE.)
evals.expected_output: Preflight probes gh readiness rather than presence: it names the active account and asks for confirmation before filing, and degrades on TRIAGE — issues are filed and labelled with existing labels only, label creation disabled — with the degradation repeated in the final report.
expectations: `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner,hasIssuesEnabled,isArchived,viewerPermission` is run and its verdict drives the decision
The multi-account case names the `Active account: true` account and asks before filing
TRIAGE degrades rather than stopping: no `gh label create` is attempted, existing labels still apply
The Preflight report shows a `⚠` row for the degraded check, and the final report repeats it
API budget is checked against the task count before any issue is created

evals.prompt: File only the first two phases of MODERNIZATION_PLAN.md as issues — I'm not ready to commit to the rest yet.
evals.expected_output: Only the named phases are filed. The epic's plan map lists every phase; excluded ones render `— not filed`. Live status comes from the sub-issues panel, not the body.
expectations: Only the named phases are filed; no issue is created for any task in an excluded phase
The map's phase table lists every phase in the plan, not just the filed ones
Excluded phases render `— not filed` in the Tasks column and list no issue numbers
The map asserts no issue status: no checkbox, progress bar, percentage, milestone verdict, or next-actionable list
Every filed child is registered as a native sub-issue of the epic, so GitHub shows its open/closed state without the body being rewritten
The epic is created once and carries the plan-binding marker, so a later run filing the remaining phases reuses it instead of creating a second epic

evals.prompt: File MODERNIZATION_PLAN.md as issues. (Run in a repo where a previous run already created the epic but was interrupted before it filed every task.)
evals.expected_output: The existing epic is found by its plan-binding marker and reused; only the tasks it does not already list are filed. No second epic is created.
expectations: The existing epic is matched on the `<!-- plan-to-issues:plan=... -->` marker, not on the dashboard sentinels
No second epic is created for the same plan path
Tasks already filed under the epic are skipped rather than duplicated
An epic carrying the `epic` label but no binding marker is offered for adoption with an explicit confirm, never adopted silently

evals.prompt: File MODERNIZATION_PLAN.md as issues, then close two of the created issues and look at the epic.
evals.expected_output: The epic's sub-issues panel shows the two as closed and its progress advances. The plan map in the body is byte-identical to what was rendered at filing time — no sync was needed.
expectations: No `/plan-to-issues sync` run is required or suggested after an issue merely closes
Re-rendering the map after the closes produces identical bytes
The epic body contains no `- [x]`, `- [ ]`, progress bar, or percentage that could contradict the closed issues
Open/closed status is readable from the epic's sub-issues panel

evals.prompt: We just talked through what needs doing to harden the ingest path. There's no plan file — turn this conversation into GitHub issues with an epic on top.
evals.expected_output: The skill resolves the conversation as its input, drafts a task list from the user's own turns, prints it and asks for confirmation before creating anything, then files one issue per confirmed task plus an epic bound with a `plan-to-issues:conversation=<slug>` marker and a `## Source` block holding the confirmed draft. The final report prints `/plan-to-issues --from-conversation --epic <n>` as the resume handle, which restores the worklist from `## Source` and files remaining tasks (no re-draft, not sync).
expectations: No plan file is required, requested, or created — `git status --porcelain` is unchanged.
The drafted task list is printed and confirmed by the user before the first mutation; declining creates nothing.
The epic body carries `<!-- plan-to-issues:conversation=<slug> -->`, a `## Source` block with the confirmed draft, and one map sentinel pair.
Each child carries `Part of #<epic>`, a label set with at least `phase:` and a type label, and is registered as a native sub-issue.
The final report prints the re-run handle `/plan-to-issues --from-conversation --epic <n>`.
That handle resumes by restoring the worklist from `## Source` (no re-draft, no confirm) and filing remaining tasks; it is not `sync`.

evals.expected_output: The arbitrary plan path is accepted with no filename special-casing: the same epic-plus-issues output as for MODERNIZATION_PLAN.md, with the epic bound to `plan-to-issues:plan=docs/ROADMAP.md`.
expectations: The skill does not look for MODERNIZATION_PLAN.md or require /codebase-modernizer to have run.
The epic binding marker names the given path, normalized repo-root-relative.
No draft-and-confirm gate runs — that gate belongs to the conversation path only.

evals.prompt: /plan-to-issues   (a plan file exists at docs/PLAN.md, and the conversation above also describes work to do)
evals.expected_output: The skill detects both possible inputs and asks the user which to convert, rather than guessing or silently merging them.
expectations: Both candidates are listed with a short summary each.
Nothing is created before the user chooses.
An explicit path argument or --from-conversation would have skipped this question.

evals.prompt: /plan-to-issues --from-conversation   (an epic already carries this conversation's slug)
evals.expected_output: The existing epic is printed and the user is asked whether to reuse it or create a new one; it is never silently reused, because a slug is not a stable identity.
expectations: The prompt names the existing epic number, title, and child count.
Reuse files only the tasks the epic does not already list; no duplicates.
`--epic <n>` binds to that epic, restores the worklist from `## Source` (no re-draft, no confirm), and files only remaining tasks.

evals.prompt: /plan-to-issues   (no plan file anywhere, and the conversation is a question about how the build works)
evals.expected_output: A `✗ No input to convert` failure on the preflight input group, naming the three ways to supply one. Nothing is created.
expectations: A question or explanation request is not treated as actionable intent.
The failure block offers a plan path, --from-conversation, and /codebase-modernizer.
Preflight reports FAIL and Phase 1 never runs.
